A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
quarterly employment rates and quarterly median earnings are the best way to benchmark program performance.

The main takeaway from our work is that
employment rates from randomized trials are not appropriate benchmarks for community programs.
the performance of supported employment programs is much more modest than is commonly assumed, and the difference in performance between the best and worst performing programs is small.
the employment rates reported by randomized trials are much larger than the rates reported by typical programs.
